notable_absence.finding: Two issues, mirroring backup-trigger-backup.md's pattern in this same batch. (1) The example uses a `full_backup` body parameter (`-d '{"full_backup": true}'`) exactly like backup-trigger-backup.md's example, but a prune operation deleting expired backups has no obvious reason to take a full-vs-incremental flag, and the page gives no explanation of what this parameter means for a PRUNE task specifically - it may be a copy-paste artifact from the backup-triggering example rather than a real prune parameter. (2) The Responses table's 200 OK row example value is `{"status":404,"msg":"repository \`res4tRepo does not exist\`"}` - a 404 error body shown as the EXAMPLE for the 200 OK success row, clearly transposed from the 400/404 rows beneath it. Both flagged as likely authoring errors rather than corrected silently.

cross_component_finding: This page's success-response shape - a JSON ARRAY containing one object (`[{"task_name": "PRUNE-..."}]`) - differs from backup-trigger-backup.md and backup-trigger-merge.md (this same batch), both of which return a single bare OBJECT (`{"task_name": "BACKUP-..."}` / `{"task_name": "MERGE-..."}`) for the structurally identical action. All three are 'trigger an immediate task now' endpoints with the same request shape (repository-id path parameter, Full Admin role, 200 OK plus a task_name), yet prune alone wraps its response in an array. Possibly because a single prune call can retroactively affect multiple expired backups and therefore may spawn more than one task, but the page never states that explanation - the asymmetry is simply there in the two worked examples, unexplained.
